clue.text: He got a different purpose for lodge

indicators.note: different says the letters of the three words before it are to be made different, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: purpose means use, as in 'what is the use of it?'

explanation.surface: A man finds a new use for a country lodge he has acquired.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatekeeper's small building at the entrance to an estate is called a lodge, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Stop and state temperature

parts.note: to state firmly is to aver

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster is told to halt and announce the temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something happening is to stop it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Move out of sight on the radio!

indicators.note: on the radio means the phrase is heard rather than seen, so it is said aloud

parts.note: EX means out of or former, and SIGHT is sight, giving 'ex-sight'

explanation.surface: A broadcaster jokes that radio puts performers out of view.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'out of sight' is rendered as EX- plus SIGHT, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone emotionally is to move them, a sense shared with thrilling or arousing them.

clue.text: Speak about number being flowery

indicators.note: about says the speaking word goes around the number abbreviation

parts.note: to speak formally is to orate

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a figure in elaborate, florid language.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowery language is elaborately decorated, which is what ornate describes.

clue.text: Review problem at university

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
UP means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A student reviews a maths problem set at college.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is a British usage for being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise or recap a discussion is to review it briefly.

clue.text: From objectors remarkably, his sympathy is actually discouraging

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the two words are arranged in a remarkable new way

explanation.surface: Comfort offered by objectors turns out to be dispiriting.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Job, Job's friends came to console him but only made him feel worse.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical phrase describes someone whose attempts at consolation only deepen distress.

clue.text: Prostrate after mishap and likely to get hurt

indicators.note: after places the prostrate word after the mishap word

parts.note: an accident is a mishap
lying prostrate is lying prone

explanation.surface: Someone lies flat after a fall, clearly liable to injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prone to accidents means tending to have mishaps and so likely to be injured.

clue.text: Shop uncovered concise memo transforming food technology

indicators.note: uncovered strips the outer letters from the word shop
transforming says the two words that follow are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shop rewrites a short memo about food technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' leaves HO from shop; 'transforming' turns CONCISE MEMO into MEECONOMICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookery and food technology form the school subject traditionally called by this name, now often renamed.

clue.text: Coldness following stiffness

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
rigidity is stiffness

explanation.surface: A chill follows a bout of stiffness in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigidity means extreme coldness, literally of temperature or figuratively of manner.

clue.text: Counting as an appraisal that could be dead first

definitions.text: an appraisal that could be dead first
definitions.meaning: dead ... is navigation by estimate, so 'dead' can come first

explanation.surface: A tally is an assessment that might be lifeless at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Calculation is counting, and a judgement or estimate is an appraisal; navigators' dead reckoning adds the word before.

clue.text: Plant once more on television

parts.note: RE means on or concerning
a television is a set

explanation.surface: A gardening programme shows plants being replanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a plant is to put it in the ground, so doing so again is a repeat setting.

clue.text: Loser might receive this as consolation

definitions.text: Loser might receive this as consolation

parts.words: Loser might receive this as consolation
parts.note: a runner-up may be given a consolation award, which looks paradoxical

explanation.surface: A defeated competitor gets something to soften the blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A consolation award is given to a runner-up, making the reward one that losers can win.

clue.text: First woman to enter the French bank

indicators.note: to enter means the first woman goes into the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: The first female customer walks into a French bank.
explanation.definitionFit: An embankment along a river to prevent flooding is a bank, as on the Mississippi.

clue.text: In this case there are no capitals

definitions.text: In this case there are no capitals

parts.words: In this case there are no capitals
parts.note: ... case letters are the small, non-capital ones, from the printers' type cases

explanation.surface: A geography fact about some region lacking capital cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers kept small letters in the bottom type case, so text without capitals is in that case.

clue.text: Jealously losing cockney female striving for superiority

indicators.note: losing says the cockney female is dropped from the jealous word

parts.note: envying, being jealous of someone
a hen is a female bird; a cockney drops the H, leaving 'en

explanation.surface: A jealous Londoner loses his girlfriend while competing for status.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, the London East End accent, drops initial H. 'Jealously' stands for envying, a stretch in part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Competing with rivals to come out on top is contending, striving for superiority.

clue.text: Chemical discovered in Leicestershire

indicators.note: discovered in says the chemical is found inside the county name

explanation.surface: A chemical has been found in an English Midlands county.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicestershire is an English county in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Esters are organic compounds formed from acids and alcohols, a class of chemical.

clue.text: Got in trouble around rocky height back in cave

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters go round the reversed hill
in trouble suggests the word got is disturbed and rearranged
back means the rocky height is read backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A climber got into difficulty on a crag before retreating to a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop, typical of Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picturesque cave, often artificial, is a grotto.

clue.text: The smallest amount give a high-pitched cry

definitions.meaning: a tiny sound or trace, as in 'not a peep'
to squeal shrilly like a mouse

explanation.surface: Even the faintest sound counts as a shrill cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse's tiny sound is a shrill cry, and 'not a peep' style usage gives a minimal amount.

clue.text: Start to watch playing this game

indicators.note: Start to picks the opening letter of watch
playing suggests the letters of this are played about with

explanation.surface: An invitation to come and watch people playing a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Whist is a card game for four players in partnerships, an example of a game.

clue.text: Corrupt female I left in river

indicators.note: in places the female, I and left letters inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A corrupted woman abandons herself in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To defile is to make impure or sully, a synonym of the verb corrupt.

clue.text: Susan turned back with heavyweight to find station

indicators.note: turned back means the short name is read backwards

parts.note: Sue is short for Susan
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: Susan retraces her steps with a burly companion to reach a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is one of London's mainline railway terminals, an example of a station.

clue.text: Fellow in agreement

definitions.meaning: a man's name, used as a generic chap
the radio word for 'message received, agreed'

explanation.surface: A colleague who is in accord.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common man's name standing for any chap, and radio operators say it to mean 'understood and agreed'.

clue.text: Troublesome Naomi embraces learner, one in the fuel industry

indicators.note: embraces says the scrambled name holds the learner letter
Troublesome suggests the name Naomi is unruly and rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: Awkward Naomi hugs a trainee who works for an oil company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troublesome' turns NAOMI into OIMAN, which takes L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works in or owns a business producing petroleum is in the fuel industry.

clue.text: Part of Mercedes, Cortina or another car

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A list of cars: Mercedes, Cortina, or some other model.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'or', a link word: 'another car' alone substitutes for the answer, which is a Ford model like the Cortina.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford Escort is a car model, so it is another car alongside the Cortina.

clue.text: Beat peculiar brother without hesitation

indicators.note: peculiar means the remaining letters are odd, rearranged
without says the hesitation sound is taken away from brother

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone thumps an odd sibling without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ER from BROTHER leaving BROTH; 'peculiar' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular pulse, as of the heart, the noun beat.

clue.text: Reportedly purchase most of the food easily

indicators.note: Reportedly means the word for purchase is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to purchase is to buy

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the food word

parts.note: fare is food, as in 'bill of fare'

explanation.surface: Buying most of the food is said to be the easiest option.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'by a great margin', which is how easily is used in 'easily the best'.

clue.text: Father with name for seductive woman

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a male parent

explanation.surface: A father names someone as a temptress.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sirens of Greek myth lured sailors with song.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythical Sirens lured sailors with song, so the word means an alluring temptress.

clue.text: Something wrong about Italian protest

indicators.note: about says the wrong deed goes around the Italian abbreviation

parts.note: a sin is a wrong act
IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: Something is wrong with an Italian demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupying a place in protest by sitting there is a form of protest demonstration.

clue.text: Conceited, I bring in a set of books

parts.note: I is the self, one's ego
to import is to bring goods in
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A vain person boasts about bringing in a collection of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an inflated sense of their own worth is vain or conceited.

clue.text: Rock having even weight

parts.note: to iron out is to make even or smooth
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A rock of balanced weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight equal to 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone is a sedimentary rock rich in iron ore, an example of rock.
